title: Time and work: practice set
sourceNote: Original practice questions written for this group. None of them is a CAT previous-year question.
instructions: 10 questions, 20 minutes, CAT marking: +3 right, -1 wrong multiple choice, 0 for a wrong type-in answer.
Type-in answers take a number only: no %, ₹ or units. Use a decimal, not a fraction.

questions.text: A can finish a job in 12 days and B can finish it in 6 days. Working together at their usual rates, how many days do they need?
A can complete a job alone in 10 days. A works for 4 days and then leaves. B finishes the rest of the job alone in 9 days. How many days would B take to do the whole job alone?
A tap fills a tank in 6 hours. An outlet pipe at the bottom can empty the full tank in 10 hours. If both are open together, how many hours does the empty tank take to fill?
12 men can build a wall in 15 days. Every man works at the same rate. How many days will 9 men need for the same wall?
A and B together can do a job in 8 days. A alone can do it in 12 days. How many days would B take alone?
A, B and C can finish a job alone in 12, 15 and 20 days. They work on it together and are paid ₹6,000 in all, shared in proportion to the work each does. How much does A get?
A can do a job in 10 days and B in 15 days. They work on alternate days, A on day 1, B on day 2, A on day 3, and so on. In how many days is the job finished?
Pipe A can fill a tank in 12 hours and pipe B can fill it in 18 hours. Both are opened together. After 4 hours pipe A is closed. How many more hours does pipe B take to fill the rest of the tank?
A is 50% more efficient than B. To do the whole job alone, A takes 10 days less than B. Working together, how many days will they take?
15 men can finish a job in 24 days. After 8 days, 5 men leave and the rest carry on at the same rate. In how many days in all, counting the first 8, is the job finished?
